title: The Many Uses of FICAR
summary: Use ficar for location, becoming, results, arrangements, remaining, and colloquial relationships.

sections.heading: Location and situatedness
sections.body: **Ficar** often means 'to be located' for relatively fixed places. It differs from **estar**, which often describes current location.

examples.en: The pharmacy is on the corner.

examples.pt: O hotel fica perto da praia.
examples.en: The hotel is near the beach.

sections.heading: Becoming and resulting state
sections.body: **Ficar + adjective/participle** expresses a change into a state or the result after something happens.

examples.en: I got tired after the trip.

examples.pt: Ela ficou feliz com a notícia.
examples.en: She became happy because of the news.

examples.pt: A porta ficou aberta a noite toda.
examples.en: The door stayed open all night.

sections.heading: Arrangements, remaining, and relationships
sections.body: Ficar also means to stay/remain, to keep something, to agree on an arrangement, or colloquially to kiss/date casually.

examples.en: I'm going to stay home today.
They hooked up at the party.

keyPoints: Ficar can mean be located, stay, become, remain, or arrange.
Ficar de + infinitive means to agree/arrange to do something.
Colloquial ficar can mean to kiss or casually date someone.

commonMistakes.note: For fixed location of a place, ficar is more natural.

commonMistakes.right: Ela virou médica. / Ela se tornou médica.
commonMistakes.note: Ficar + noun is limited; becoming a profession uses virar/se tornar.
